justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across time horizons, anchored around a current level near 72. For the 1-day estimate of 72.1, I was essentially assuming near-term mean reversion and continuity — whatever the asset or indicator is trading at currently, it is unlikely to move dramatically in a single session absent a specific catalyst, so the estimate hugs the last known value closely. The 1-week estimate of 72.5 reflects a slight positive drift assumption, perhaps based on a mild underlying trend or momentum signal. The 1-month estimate of 73.5 extends that drift further, implying a slow grind higher over the medium term, though with considerably more uncertainty baked in given the longer time window.

The confidence interval widths expand substantially as the horizon lengthens, which reflects standard uncertainty compounding. For the 1-day window, a 90% CI of roughly 70.2 to 74.0 implies relatively tight bounds consistent with typical daily volatility. By one week, the interval widens to 68.8–76.2, acknowledging that multi-session moves can accumulate meaningfully. The 1-month interval of 65.5–81.5 is quite wide, reflecting the reality that over four weeks, macro developments, sentiment shifts, or structural changes can substantially reprice the underlying. The width also reflects model uncertainty — my confidence in the drift assumption itself decreases as the horizon extends.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, an unexpected macro shock — a surprise central bank decision, a geopolitical escalation, or a deterioration in risk sentiment — could drive the value well below 65.5 within a month. Liquidity events or technical breakdowns could accelerate selling beyond what historical volatility would suggest. On the upside, a positive catalyst such as a strong data release, policy easing signal, or short-covering squeeze could push the value above 81.5 more quickly than the model anticipates.

It is also worth noting that my intervals assume a relatively stable volatility regime. If realized volatility were to spike — as it does during crisis periods — even the 1-day interval could prove too narrow. The stated 90% CI means I expect roughly a 1-in-10 chance of the outcome falling outside those bounds, but fat-tailed distributions in financial or real-world data mean the true probability of extreme outcomes may be higher than classical models suggest.
